key_insight: G-Retriever’s graph tokens become nearly indistinguishable across inputs, functioning primarily as a generic soft prompt rather than conveying graph-specific information.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate graph-token use with controlled interventions rather than task accuracy alone, since a learned constant prompt can match or outperform graph-conditioned prompting.
method: Analyze token collapse across graph encoders, LLM families, and adaptation settings.
Replace graph tokens with dataset means, other examples’ tokens, or corrupted-graph tokens.
Test a two-stage procedure for producing non-collapsed tokens and probe what information they encode.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmarks, three graph encoders, two LLM families, and frozen and LoRA-adapted models, token substitutions produced no resolved answer-accuracy effect under the standard setup.
watch_item: Non-collapsed tokens do not establish graph use: they may encode question information or answer priors, and the LLM may ignore graph-derived content.
paper_title: On the Token Collapse Phenomenon in Textual Graph Soft Prompting
